mcq.question: Why must a rename refactoring work on tokens instead of plain text?

options.A: So that strings, comments and longer identifiers containing the old name are left unchanged
options.C: Because compilers cannot read renamed files
options.D: Because identifiers are case-insensitive in C++

mcq.explanation: A text replace of `total` also changes `total_count` and the word inside `"total"`. Only whole identifier tokens that refer to the symbol should change.

mcq.question: Which CLion shortcut finds all references to a symbol on Windows, according to the cheat-sheet?
mcq.explanation: In CLion's default Windows keymap, Alt+F7 is Find Usages. Shift+F6 renames, Ctrl+B goes to the declaration and Ctrl+F8 toggles a breakpoint.

bonus.question: A real IDE uses a full C++ front end (clangd) to resolve which declaration each name refers to. Give an example where the token-based rename in this lesson would still rename the wrong thing.
Write a failing test showing that `find_references` ignores a name inside a raw string literal `R"(total)"`, then extend the tokenizer to handle raw strings.
